chapter: Day jobs and Bay Area gigs
title: WPA, shoe shop jobs and Caterpillar
summary: He worked on WPA, then shoe repair, then Caterpillar from 1942, while gigging at Sweets Ballroom with Ben Watkins.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: so you were there you toured around with Ben Watkins and a bunch of other bands

then I started on the WPA I got a job on the WPA at the last minute I said well I can't make it here well you out of the you are doing pretty good with your eyes so I think I'll go to Chicago I had friends that in Chicago that was the late Joey DeRiley he was a drummer on the band and the late Ransom Nolan he was a bass player a bass player Ransom Nolan K-N-O-W-L-I-N-G and he was in Chicago at the time so I said well I think I'll go to Chicago and I'll look up Joey's Riley so at that time I had applied for the WPA and I had a little bad time it gave me a bad time of giving me a job giving me a job there because there was only this guy said I wasn't from the state of California so I told him I was a citizen of the United States and I understood that the work progress of the industry so that applied to all citizens regardless of where you're from so anyhow he saw my point and I didn't get a he said well I have nothing open for music I said I don't care what it is the only thing I want to work right now so I helped to slope those hills over there by the Broadway tunnel I helped my initial subway route up there

I got a job working for Zinkes Zinkes? Z-I-N-K-E-S Zinkes Zinkes it was on Washington between 12th and 13th by that time the old Smith it was Money Back Smith and Marlon opened his jewelry later on mmm back about 30 what 39 yeah about 39 or 40 I worked in there I worked there so I was shining and redoing shoes I would reswade shoes I learned a lot about shoes about how to change the color of shoes and how to spray the felt on shoes to make it raise up and how to dye them in different colors like white shoes we could dye them yellow or green or blue in other words people used to bring in the ladies used to bring in a part of the dress just a little clipping of the dress and dye the shoes to match the dress and we had to do that it was kind of technical
so I learned how to do that

and I left there and I worked for Crest at 14 and Broadway yeah and when the war started I uh, by 1942 I left there and I had a brother Joseph Fleming working for Caterpillar Tractor Company Caterpillar Tractor Company

so I went to work for Caterpillar Tractor Company and I worked there for 36 years but working at Caterpillar during that time I played at Sweets Ballroom with the Ben Watkins band I played there Sunday for the Mexican Mexican and I played Monday night for the dances uh, we did that for about all three years at Sweets Ballroom with Ben Watkins Orchestra

you had these day jobs or working at Crest's or something like that but did that bother you that you couldn't make a living totally out of playing music was it kind of interesting to you that you were learning something new? was that it? no it didn't bother me

because I was able to gig a little bit by gigging a little bit on the side I was making a little money to keep going and so this um, kept my standard of living of going to the part where I didn't have to be those things like that
yeah, well you didn't have to what? well those were tough times into the depression the late 30s
